paper_metadata.title: Towards An End-To-End Approach For Quantum Principal Component Analysis

experiments.description: Ideal-simulator quantum PCA experiment for a 2x2 synthetic covariance matrix in an interest-rate-risk setting, using phase estimation to estimate eigenvalues and a tomography-style sign estimation circuit to reconstruct principal components.

algorithm.variant: Quantum PCA with phase estimation plus extended quantum state tomography for complex amplitudes

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Input covariance matrix A is encoded into registers M and E; register M uses 2 qubits for the 2x2 matrix, and register E uses 2 qubits for phase estimation.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Extract eigenvalues and eigenvectors (principal components) of the covariance matrix via quantum phase estimation and tomography.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Matrix trace normalization is assumed in the general method; for the experiment, a synthetic covariance matrix is used directly as the test instance.

problem_instance.description: Synthetic 2x2 covariance matrix for two hypothetical assets in an interest-rate-risk style PCA use case.

dataset_specification.description: Matrix A = [[0.6507, 0.2122], [0.2122, 0.3493]]; generated from 1000 simulated return scenarios for each asset over one year; validated by domain experts.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Daily differences among tenors are conceptually described; for the synthetic experiment, 1000 simulated return scenarios were used to build the covariance matrix.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Ideal simulation on IBM qasm simulator; results inspected via counts for phase estimation and sign estimation circuits.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Synthetic covariance matrix generation; in the general method, trace normalization is applied if tr(A) != 1.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Aggregate measured probabilities by eigenvalue register, identify local maxima as eigenvalues, and reconstruct eigenvectors from the measured output distribution.

speedup_claims.baseline_method: classical PCA / classical linear algebra methods
speedup_claims.conditions: for low-rank density matrices under the quantum PCA framework of Lloyd et al.; asymptotic fault-tolerant setting
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper does not provide an empirical classical-vs-quantum runtime comparison; the advantage is cited from prior work and remains theoretical in this implementation.

speedup_claims.factor: O(log(N^2)) initialization; O(t^2 epsilon^-1 log(N^2)) Hamiltonian simulation; O((36 d ln d / delta^2) t^2 epsilon^-1 log(N^2)) tomography
speedup_claims.conditions: low-rank matrix assumption for Hamiltonian simulation; tomography sample complexity depends on state dimension d and error parameter delta
speedup_claims.caveats: These are complexity expressions, not measured speedups.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Initialization O(log(N^2)); Hamiltonian simulation / unitary construction O(t^2 epsilon^-1 log(N^2)); phase estimation dominated by O(t^2 epsilon^-1 log(N^2)); tomography O((36 d ln d / delta^2) t^2 epsilon^-1 log(N^2))

experiments.description: Real-device quantum PCA experiment on IBM Perth for the same 2x2 synthetic covariance matrix, evaluating phase estimation and sign estimation under hardware noise/decoherence.

algorithm.variant: Quantum PCA with phase estimation plus extended quantum state tomography for complex amplitudes

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Input covariance matrix A is encoded into registers M and E; sign estimation adds one control qubit.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Extract eigenvalues and eigenvectors of the covariance matrix.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Same as the simulator experiment; sign estimation uses post-selection on control qubit = 0.

problem_instance.description: Same synthetic 2x2 covariance matrix used in the simulator experiment.

dataset_specification.description: Matrix A = [[0.6507, 0.2122], [0.2122, 0.3493]]; generated from 1000 simulated return scenarios for each asset over one year; validated by domain experts.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Synthetic covariance construction from simulated returns; no additional preprocessing details reported for the QPU run.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Executed on IBM Perth; compared qualitatively against ideal-simulator results for amplitude estimation and sign estimation.

noise_model.noise_description: hardware noise / decoherence on real QPU

implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Same postprocessing as simulator experiment; results noted to degrade for the deeper sign circuit due to decoherence.

speedup_claims.baseline_method: classical PCA / classical linear algebra methods
speedup_claims.conditions: same as the simulator experiment; theoretical quantum PCA framework
speedup_claims.caveats: No empirical speedup is shown on hardware; the paper reports qualitative degradation in the sign-estimation circuit due to decoherence.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Initialization O(log(N^2)); Hamiltonian simulation / unitary construction O(t^2 epsilon^-1 log(N^2)); phase estimation dominated by O(t^2 epsilon^-1 log(N^2)); tomography O((36 d ln d / delta^2) t^2 epsilon^-1 log(N^2))
